html:
The Tumbalalá are an Indigenous people of the dry backlands of northern Bahia, Brazil, on the São Francisco River near Abaré and Curaçá.

They descend from peoples gathered in colonial missions on the river islands, who later lost their land and language and lived as rural workers. In the late 1990s they asked to be recognised as an Indigenous people again, one of many such "resurgent" peoples of northeast Brazil, and their land claim followed. They hold the toré ritual dance, shared with neighbours such as the Pankararu and Atikum. The area belongs to the region of the Brazilian sertão, long ruled by cattle ranchers.
sum: The Tumbalalá are an Indigenous people of the dry backlands of northern Bahia, Brazil, on the São Francisco River near Abaré and Curaçá.
